chunks: And from him, from Abbas, from Rifah, who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'When he has completed eight circuits, let him complete fourteen.' I asked: 'Does he pray four rak'at?' He said: 'He prays two rak'at.'
And that which indicates what we mentioned, that he only completes fourteen circuits when his action is done on the basis of forgetfulness, is what has been narrated:
ai.seo_question: How many rak'at are prayed during the eight circuits of Tawaf al-Qudum according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific practice of Imam Ali (AS) regarding the two-rak'at prayer following the four circuits of Tawaf al-Qudum, distinguishing it from the full four-rak'at prayer associated with other circumambations. The text highlights the nuance of 'nسيان' (forgetfulness or customary habit) to explain why the shorter prayer is observed, reflecting the scholarly debate on whether this was a specific Sunnah of the Prophet or a practice of the Imams. It underscores the precision in Shia fiqh regarding the distinction between obligatory acts and recommended customs during Hajj rituals.
